newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel rejects Clinton anti-smoking funds.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel rejects Clinton anti-smoking funds.

text.p: A Senate Appropriations subcommittee on Tuesday declined to recommend funds for a Clinton administration initiative aimed at enforcing anti-teen smoking regulations.

On a voice vote, the Senate Appropriations subcommittee on agriculture passed a $50.5 billion spending bill for the Agriculture Department and Food and Drug Administration programs, but included no funds for the initiative.
Last week, the House Appropriations Committee approved $24.3 million for FDA anti-smoking enforcement activities, about $10 million below the Clinton administration's request.

After Tuesday's meeting, subcommittee Chairman Thad Cochran, a Mississippi Republican, said funding for the FDA enforcement activities should instead come from the proposed $368 billion settlement that state attorney generals reached with tobacco companies last month.
Failing that, Congress would have another chance to deal with the issue as part of an FDA reform bill that has been introduced in the Senate, he said.
"We're assuming that one or both of them will reach fruition sometime soon," he said.
Cochran said he was "reluctant" to appropriate funds to the states in the form of grants for anti-smoking enforcement activities.
"Our position is 'let the states do it with their own money,'" he said. He noted that Mississippi has just won a huge settlement with tobacco companies that should provide funds for such activities.
The full Senate appropriations committee will meet Thursday on the FY98 spending bill. In addition, the House is expected to take up the agriculture and FDA spending package this week.
